title: The Otter Blocks WordPress plugin before 3.2.3 does not validate that a user-supplied return URL belongs to the site before using it to build the… (CVE-2026-109937)
description: The Otter Blocks WordPress plugin versions before 3.2.3 contain a vulnerability where the plugin does not verify that a user-supplied return URL is part of the same site before using it in a Stripe Checkout session. This flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to redirect users who complete or cancel checkout to arbitrary external URLs. The vulnerability has a medium severity with a CVSS score of 5.4.
aiSummary: The Otter Blocks WordPress plugin prior to version 3.2.3 fails to validate that a user-supplied return URL belongs to the same site before incorporating it as the return destination in a Stripe Checkout session. This improper validation can be exploited by unauthenticated attackers to redirect users to arbitrary external URLs after they complete or cancel a checkout process, potentially facilitating phishing or other malicious redirection attacks.
aiImpact: An attacker can cause users to be redirected to arbitrary external URLs after completing or canceling a Stripe Checkout session. This could be used for phishing or redirecting users to malicious sites. There is no indication of direct compromise of the site or user data beyond the redirection. The vulnerability requires user interaction (UI:R) and has no privileges required (PR:N).
